text.content:
Derangements represent lasting mental instability brought on by overwhelming terror, guilt, or trauma (or, for Malkavians, the Clan Disadvantage). Each derangement has a trigger; once triggered, its effects last for the rest of the scene. A character can resist a single triggering by spending a Willpower Trait, which holds off the derangement for that scene — if the trigger persists into the next scene, another Willpower Trait is needed. Derangements should only be taken with Storyteller consultation, and a character's derangement always feels entirely rational from the inside; this is advanced roleplaying material, not comic relief.

The Derangements

  • Bulimia: Stress drives the character to gorge on blood (or food) past any real need, then purge and gorge again. Must test Conscience/Conviction when feeding; failure means feeding to a full blood pool regardless of need. Being kept from feeding forces a frenzy check.
  • Crimson Rage: Fits of anger from the character's own helplessness, not the Beast — though it doesn't protect against an actual frenzy. Grants Negative Traits Violent x2 and Impatient while active.
  • Fugue: Severe stress triggers blackouts. A failed Static Willpower Challenge against the stress hands control of the character to the Narrator for a scene, during which she acts to relieve the stress; the character wakes afterward with no memory of it.
  • Hysteria: Wild mood swings and violent outbursts under pressure. The character must resist frenzy whenever stressed, and an especially dramatic failure triggers automatic frenzy.
  • Immortal Terror: An unconscious death wish born from confronting the true weight of eternity. Direct evidence of the character's immortality (a funeral, a mortal ally's death) forces a Static Willpower Challenge (difficulty four) or the character pursues genuinely dangerous, even Masquerade-breaking, behavior without consciously realizing why.
  • Manic-Depression: Failing a personal goal forces a Static Willpower Challenge or the character spirals into depression for several scenes (halved Willpower for comparisons, no spending Blood Traits to boost Physical Traits), followed by an equal period of obsessive mania during which she is one Trait down resisting frenzy.
  • Megalomania: An all-consuming need for dominance. One Trait up on Willpower tests while active, but must win a Willpower test (difficulty six) to resist any opportunity to commit diablerie during that time.
  • Multiple Personalities: Trauma fractures the psyche into distinct personas, each tied to the trauma that spawned it and triggered by relevant circumstances; each persona's Traits must still be purchased normally and worked out with the Storyteller.
  • Obsessive/Compulsive: A fixation on controlling one aspect of life or repeating a specific ritual action. One Trait up resisting Dominate or coercion away from the behavior, but frenzies automatically if forcibly prevented from it.
  • Paranoia: Conviction that all suffering stems from hidden enemies. One Trait down on all Social tests while active, and any sign of suspicious activity forces a frenzy check.
  • Regression: Retreating to a childlike state to avoid responsibility. Two Traits down on all Mental Challenges.
  • Sanguinary Animism: Guilt over feeding manifests as imagined memories and a victim's voice. Feeding on a mortal forces a Static Willpower Challenge; success means one Trait down on all challenges for the scene, failure spawns a hostile second personality that imposes a one-Trait penalty to all actions until dawn.
  • Schizophrenia: The psyche fractures around unresolved inner conflict, producing hallucinations and unpredictable behavior tied to the original trauma. Must automatically retest any won frenzy-resistance check, and is two Traits down on all Willpower tests.
